title: Mutating Structs Inside a List
statement:
A `struct` is a value type: every time one is read out of somewhere --
assigned to a variable, passed to a method, returned from an indexer --
what you get is a *copy*. That is invisible and harmless right up until
the somewhere it was read out of is a `List<T>`, and the whole point was
to change the original.

## The type

```
public struct Counter
{
    public int Value;
    public void Increment() { Value++; }
}
```

`Counter` is a mutable struct: `Increment()` changes `Value` on whatever
`Counter` it is called on.

## Your function

```
public static void IncrementAll(List<Counter> counters);
```

Call `Increment()` on every element of `counters`, **mutating the list in
place** -- after this function returns, `counters[i].Value` must be one
greater than it was before, for every `i`.

## Watch out

- **`counters[i].Increment();` compiles cleanly and does nothing to the
  list.** `List<T>`'s indexer getter returns a *copy* of the struct at
  that position -- `counters[i]` is a value, not a reference to the slot
  it came from -- so `Increment()` mutates that copy, which is then
  discarded the moment the statement ends. No warning, no exception: the
  list is silently unchanged.
- **`foreach (var c in counters) { c.Increment(); }` has exactly the same
  problem** -- `c` is a fresh copy on every iteration, not a window onto
  the list's own storage, so mutating it mutates nothing the caller can
  see afterwards.
- **The fix is read, mutate, write back, explicitly**: read the struct out
  of the list into a local variable, call `Increment()` on the *local*,
  then assign the local back into the list at the same index. Three
  separate steps, because the read and the write are the only two
  operations that actually touch the list's own storage -- the mutation in
  between only ever touches the local copy.

tests.description: IncrementAll is called three times in a row -- a solution that mutates a temporary and discards it reports '0 10' unchanged, whichever round is checked.
